claims.text: High-entropy alloys containing multiple principal elements and oxide- or nitride-forming alloying elements will have superior tribo-corrosion resistance compared with traditional structural alloys.
The initial material is prone to degradation under combined elevated-temperature and tribo-corrosion conditions.
Adding oxide- or nitride-forming alloying elements to HEAs promotes formation of protective surface layers.
The resulting surface layers are stable oxides or nitrides.
Alloying elements in HEAs react with the environment to form the proposed oxide or nitride layers.
The stable oxide or nitride layers protect the HEA surface and reduce degradation.
The proposed HEAs will show a 30% lower degradation rate than traditional structural alloys.
The proposed advantage applies at temperatures of 500–800 °C, a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s, and a normal load of 10 N.
Degradation resistance may vary with HEA composition and the severity of the tribo-corrosion conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a 30% reduction, but the falsification rule only requires a 20% reduction; an observed reduction of 20–29% would fail to achieve the stated prediction while still not falsifying the hypothesis.
